definition: Professional development is the ongoing process of building and maintaining the knowledge, competence, and skills needed for advanced practice. In this packet, it is described as continuing development that is expected alongside activities such as mentoring, research, and publication.

provenance.scope: Source record C20835; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports that continuing professional development is expected, but not the broader definition of professional development as an ongoing process of building and maintaining knowledge, competence, and skills.

The phrase about being expected alongside mentoring, research, and publication is only partially supported; the packet lists research, publications, mentoring, and continuing professional development as expected skill sets, but does not frame them as a package or define professional development in relation to them.
The definition adds an advanced-practice gloss that is not stated in the packet and goes beyond the supplied text.

The packet does not state that professional development is an “ongoing process of building and maintaining” knowledge/competence/skills; it only notes that “continuing professional development” is an “expected skill set.”

The packet supports “advanced” practice context and mentions research/publications/mentoring/continuing professional development as expected, but it does not support the broader phrasing that this development is “needed for advanced practice” as a general definition.

The packet’s content is specifically about “advanced diabetes practice” (Diabetes Management Nurse Specialist) rather than establishing the term in the field of “counselling skills,” beyond mentioning counseling in the clinical scope rather than defining professional development for counselling.
